text:
Arun: bringing up sparrow11b (mistral-like head layout, qwen-style proj packing) in int4. short ctx looks within noise but long-context coherency drops after ~400-600 tokens. not classic eos-drop — more of a collapse to boilerplate repeats.
Lina: did you use symmetric quant or the profile-aware asymmetric we added? small zero-point mismatch can create a drift over autoreg steps.
Arun: used converter default which is symmetric-per-tensor. command: `./convert --src sparrow11b.bin --out sparrow11b.int4 --profile medium --perchannel=false`
Jorge: also check the kv-cache write/read ordering. if proj packing differs between q/k/v blocks we sometimes write kv segments in a different head-order so later reads scramble cross-head dot products.
Maya: what about rotary parameters? some exports change rotary base frequency or include an extra cos scaling. that can look like temperature shift rather than immediate token swap.
Arun: good points. I dumped a short diff of logits vs fp16 on the same seed. early tokens align; KL starts creeping up around step 30. attaching snippet below.
Lina: try rerun with `--perchannel=true` and `--zero_point=auto` to capture asymmetric bias. also flip `--proj_packing=detect` if available.
Arun: trick: the converter has a debugging flag `--dump-qkv-layout` which prints offsets. here's output for this build: `q_offset=0, k_offset=96, v_offset=192, block_stride=256, head_dim=64`. looks gemma-like but our reference expects v_offset before k in the packed proj (q,v,k).
Jorge: aha. that ordering mismatch would silently corrupt attention when we split the packed block into q/k/v. In int4 we mask values into nibble pairs so an offset flip can produce systematic bias across heads.
Maya: try re-export with `--proj-order=qvk` or set converter to reorder after reading raw weights. We also had luck with a post-conversion pass that swaps k/v blocks on the file level.
Arun: will test two runs: (A) reorder at conversion `--proj-order=qvk --force-transpose` and (B) keep order but run eval with fp16 kernel but int4 params to isolate quantization error.
Lina: for (B) also run a KV-warmup-only pass (feed large static context but stop before generation) to see if weights diverge during cache accumulation vs generation.
Arun: scheduling both now. commands I'm running: `./convert --src sparrow11b.bin --out a.int4 --proj-order=qvk --perchannel=true` then `./eval --model a.int4 --task longcont --seed 7 --log-steps 25`. second run: `./eval --model sparrow11b.int4 --kernel fp16 --seed 7 --log-steps 25`
Jorge: if fp16 kernel with int4 weights still drifts then packing or rotary is wrong. if it matches fp16 ref then quant error is likely.
Maya: extra check: compare pre-softmax norms of attention logits per head across steps. if one head systematically gains norm that's sign of k-v misalignment; if norms similar but softmax sharpens, look at rotary scale.
Arun: triage-bot asked to create a ticket. will attach the conv logs, qkv-dump, and KL-trace. triage-bot: Please open ticket with label=eng-ml/interop and include `model:sparrow11b seed:7 priority:high`
triage-bot: Ticket created: INC-2026. Linking artifacts at /mnt/eng-ml/sparrow11b/INC-2026/ (contains qkv-layout.txt, kl_trace.csv, logits_diff.tar.gz).
Lina: thanks. once we have diffs, if it's proj packing we can add a small heuristic in loader: peek at packed weight magic bytes and infer ordering 90% of the time. saves manual flags.
Arun: will post results in this thread when runs finish. keeping short logs in /tmp/sparrow-quick. :memo:
